_why: The merge policy for this repository, in version control, because it was not.
docs/DISPATCH-READINESS.md described these settings from memory and omitted
substrate-guard from the required checks. Nothing caught it, because the
settings lived only in the GitHub UI where no reviewer sees them and no diff
shows a change. That is the failure gh-aw's ADR-27193 predicted when it
rejected 'rely on branch-protection settings' as making policy 'invisible to
code reviewers and hard to version-control'.
This file is the declared policy. tests/test_branch_protection_policy.py
asserts the docs agree with it, so the drift that happened cannot happen
silently again. Verifying the LIVE settings against this file needs network
and auth, so it is a manual check, documented below.
_enforce_admins_why: Deliberately off. GitHub forbids approving your own PR, so with admin
enforcement on a solo owner could never merge and the repo would deadlock
The cost: every merge here needs --admin, including docs-only ones, so the
override carries no information about WHY it was used. That is BRE-18, not a
flaw in this setting. A second identity restores the signal.
A GitHub App is not an admin and has no such escape hatch. Do NOT grant the
App an admin bypass, or every control here becomes decorative.
_substrate_guard_why: substrate-guard is REQUIRED and can never pass on a PR that touches
_HARNESS_PATHS, whether the change strengthens the harness or weakens it.
So a substrate PR has no normal merge path and --admin is the intended
That is the point: the override is tied to repo admin permission, which the
agent identity will never hold. An approval, or a magic string in a PR body,
can be produced by anything that can write. This cannot.
